title: Tap to Reveal Controls — Video / Recorded Live Stream

user_story.role: community member watching a video or recorded live stream
user_story.action: have tapping the player surface reveal the controls instead of toggling pause
user_story.value: not accidentally interrupt playback during normal viewing

invest_check._note: Small resolved by the UC1a/UC1b component split (STEP1).

preconditions: User is viewing a video post or recorded live stream on any in-scope surface
entry_points: A. Video / recorded LS playing inline in any feed (global, user, community, event discussion)
B. Video / recorded LS open in a media gallery or fullscreen view

not_supported: Desktop — UI-only (button size), no behaviour change; first tap = 1-Step Pause (BR-09)

business_rules.statement: Seek/skip (±10s) controls exist only on a video or recorded live stream — never on an active Live stream.
The controls overlay auto-dismisses after 1 second of no interaction while playing; the countdown restarts on every control interaction.
The controls behaviour is identical across all in-scope surfaces (surface-invariant; NOT platform-invariant).
First-tap interaction model is platform-dependent: mobile reveals controls without toggling playback; desktop (Web UIKit) is a direct 1-step pause/play.
Play/pause state changes only via an explicit user pause/play action (BR-09) or a terminal room state (BR-12) — no implicit operation toggles it.
While playing the overlay auto-dismisses (BR-03); while paused it persists and dismisses only on a tap outside the play button, and the media stays paused.
Resume target by media type: video/recorded resumes from the exact paused position; Live resumes at the current live edge.
The viewer is never left on a frozen frame with no feedback — any interruption surfaces an explicit state.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Tap playing player → controls appear, playback continues (mobile)
given: a video or recorded live stream is playing on a mobile surface (iOS / Android / web-on-mobile)
the controls overlay is currently hidden
acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps anywhere on the player surface
then: the controls overlay appears
playback continues uninterrupted — the media does not pause
the central button shows the pause icon (reflecting the playing state)
acceptance_criteria._platform_variance: Desktop (Web UIKit) = 1-Step Pause: the first tap pauses directly; this AC (reveal, no pause) is the MOBILE behaviour (BR-09). Test expected split by form factor — see platform-behavior-notes.md PV-1.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Tap outside button (playing) → overlay dismisses, playback continues
acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps the player surface outside the central pause/play button's tap target
then: the overlay dismisses
playback continues uninterrupted

acceptance_criteria.when: the user takes no further action for 1 second
then: the overlay auto-dismisses
playback continues
acceptance_criteria._delta: web currently 3s (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70) — must change to 1s per BR-03.

given: a video or recorded live stream is playing
acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps the central pause button
then: playback pauses at the current position
the button icon switches pause→play and remains visible

tapping anywhere outside the play button dismisses the overlay — the media stays paused

acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps the central play button
then: playback resumes from the exact position at which it was paused

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Behaviour identical across all in-scope surfaces
given: any in-scope surface (global / user / community / event-discussion feed, media gallery, fullscreen)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user performs any of AC-01…AC-05
then: the behaviour is identical regardless of surface
acceptance_criteria._note: surface-invariant ≠ platform-invariant — mobile vs desktop still differ (BR-09).

given: a video or recorded live stream is actively playing on any in-scope surface
acceptance_criteria.when: the post first renders and no tap has occurred yet
then: no controls overlay is shown — only the media surface is visible

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Idle timer resets on control interaction
given: the user interacts with an overlay control (volume/scrubber) before the 1s timeout elapses
then: the 1s idle countdown restarts — the overlay does not disappear while the user is interacting
after the last interaction the overlay auto-dismisses 1s later; playback continues throughout

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Pause tap coincides with auto-dismiss timer firing
given: the 1s idle timer is about to fire
acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps the central pause button at that instant
then: playback pauses
the play icon is shown and persists — it is not caught by the expiring timer
the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside

given: the media is buffering (not yet playing)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user taps the player surface
then: the overlay appears
the central button reflects the real state (loading/paused) — not a false 'playing' icon
no crash or frozen overlay; the icon updates once playback starts

acceptance_criteria.scenario: App backgrounded during an active overlay/timer (OS default)
given: the controls overlay is visible (playing or paused)
acceptance_criteria.when: the user returns the app to the foreground
then: the player/overlay reach a well-defined state via the OS default (Option 1, code-grounded)
iOS: the OS paused the media on background and does not auto-resume; the wall-clock 1s timer already elapsed so a playing overlay is dismissed and a paused overlay persists
no stale mid-countdown overlay
acceptance_criteria._decision: Option 1 (adopt OS default) — see ac-authoring.md AC-11 + platform-behavior-notes.md Code-verified notes.
